discovery: Cavity optomechanics: quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion by light

nominees.name: Tobias J. Kippenberg
nominees.affiliation: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austria

motivation: The nominees made cavity optomechanics an experimental field. Their work showed that radiation pressure inside high-finesse optical and microwave cavities can cool, amplify, squeeze and entangle the motion of engineered mechanical resonators. Kippenberg demonstrated radiation-pressure dynamical backaction and sideband cooling in microtoroids. Aspelmeyer pioneered self-cooling of micromirrors, strong optomechanical coupling and the quantum control of levitated nanoparticles in their motional ground state. Painter's optomechanical crystals brought a mechanical resonator to its quantum ground state using laser cooling and showed quantum-coherent conversion between photons and phonons. Together these experiments brought objects containing billions of atoms into the quantum regime and reached measurement imprecision at the standard quantum limit. They also produced lasting tools: displacement and force sensing beyond classical limits, microwave-to-optical transducers for superconducting quantum processors, and new tests of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales.
